chunk_findings.detail: The tick decides whether an entry is overdue by calling `time.time()` directly, and the module’s own `start_integrator(..., now=...)` parameter is ignored. In a fake-clock environment (which the project guidance requires for clocks [r-adapters]), this makes the tick use the host wall clock instead of the injected clock: for example, with `[merge_queue].auto_run_after_s = 1`, an entry released at fake time `1000` and a fake/`TickCtx` time of `1002`, but a host wall clock of `0`, `LR.overdue(..., time.time())` sees no overdue entry and the tick returns `None`, so the integrator is not started; conversely, a host wall clock far ahead can start it too early.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:integrator_tick

chunk_findings.detail: These two new knobs are not org-lockable as written because they omit `strictest`, unlike the adjacent `auto_run` knob; [r-everything-configurable] requires knobs to be org-lockable. A project can therefore set `auto_run_after_s = 0` or `auto_run_max_parallel = 10` even when an org policy needs to forbid immediate auto-starts or more than one live integrator job, and the org has no strictest value to lock them to.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:auto_run_after_s, auto_run_max_parallel

chunk_findings.detail: The integrator-job detection strips shell quoting before comparing. `integrator_command()` builds a shell-quoted command with `shlex.join()`, but `live_jobs()` then does `shlex.split(...)[3:]` and `" ".join(...)`, which removes the quoting around the repo path. For a repo path containing spaces, e.g. `repo=Path("/tmp/my repo")`, the stored command ends with `--repo '/tmp/my repo' --agent integrator queue run`, while `tail` is `--repo /tmp/my repo --agent integrator queue run`; `j.command.endswith(tail)` is false even for a live integrator job. Then `integrator_alive()` can report false while an integrator job is running but not holding the queue lock, producing a false “integrator not running” warning and potentially causing the tick to start another integrator.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:live_jobs

chunk_findings.detail: The first warning line claims the listed names are released entries, but it names arbitrary overdue queued entries. For example, if `overdue()` returns two entries, `itemA` with `released=False` and `itemB` with `released=True`, and no integrator is alive, `rel` has length 1 but `names` is `"itemA, itemB"`, so the warning says `2 entries waiting (1 released: itemA, itemB)`, falsely presenting `itemA` as released. The same code also emits a nonempty warning with `0 released: ...` when there are overdue queued entries but none are released, despite the stated purpose being a warning about released entries waiting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:warning

chunk_findings.detail: This new code bypasses adapter ports for external dependencies: `integrator_command()` uses `sys.executable` directly to determine the interpreter/environment, and `overdue()` uses `time.time()` directly for the clock. Under [r-adapters], clocks and environment access should go through the adapter ports so tests and swaps can replace them without changing service code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:integrator_command [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not request the `on` fixture, while this change adds `_no_auto_integrator` to `tests/conftest.py` to keep auto-integration off by default. It monkeypatches `MS.time` to `queued_at + 1` and asserts `MS.integrator_tick(ctx) is None`. Under the disabled auto-run state, that `None` can be produced simply because auto-run is off, not because the entry is correctly not overdue. For example, if `auto_run_after_s` were changed to `0` or the tick body ignored the threshold but the tick were still gated by the disabled knob, this test would still pass, so it does not actually prove the wait behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:test_the_tick_waits_until_the_entry_is_overdue

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion is `assert _queue_block(rp, st, cfg) == "" or "integrator not running" in _queue_block(rp, st, cfg)`. The first disjunct is true whenever the brief omits the queue warning entirely, so the test passes even if `_queue_block` returns no warning. The intent requires brief output to say that released entries are waiting and name the next call; this assertion cannot detect a missing brief warning. Concretely, if `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py::_queue_block` is changed to return `""` for this overdue, integrator-less state, the test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:test_a_wait_with_nobody_integrating_is_a_warning_with_the_next_call

chunk_findings.detail: The “fake” job launcher still creates a real OS subprocess: `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`. [r-adapters] says tests should use a fake instead of subprocesses. In a CI sandbox or container where child process creation is restricted, every test using `procs` fails inside `fake_launch` with an OS error, even though the ddflow code under test is not at fault; it also makes job liveness depend on real process scheduling rather than a fake clock/adapter.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:procs

chunk_findings.detail: `integrator_tick` calls `time.time()` directly rather than using the clock port or the injected clock from `TickCtx`/the existing `now` argument on `start_integrator`. A tick running with a fake clock set ahead past `[merge_queue].auto_run_after_s` will pass the real wall clock to `LR.overdue`, so `overdue` returns false and a dead integrator is not restarted; the promised fake-clock tick test cannot drive the dead-job restart. This also violates the clock-port requirement in `r-adapters`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:73 [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `strictest=("off", "ddflow starts no process on its own; the queue is run by hand")` passes a 2-tuple where `knob` expects the strictest allowed value to be one of the `choices` values, i.e. the string `"off"`. Running any `ddflow` command that loads this config in strict mode (or any config validation that checks `strictest in choices`) will either fail because `('off', '...')` is not in `("on", "off")`, or it will store a strictest value that is not recognized as `"off"`, so the knob is not actually forced off as intended.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The warning computes `rel` as the released waiting entries but computes `names` from `waiting[:NAMED]`, not from `rel`. So it names entries that are not released. Given one released entry `A` and one ready but not released entry `B`, both `QUEUED` longer than `auto_run_after_s` with no integrator alive, the output is `2 entries waiting (1 released: A, B), integrator not running...`, reporting `B` as released. If the first five waiting entries are ready and the only released entry appears later, the message names no released entry at all while still giving a nonzero released count. This contradicts the required “N released entries waiting” warning and misleads the operator about which entry is released.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:warning

chunk_findings.detail: `tail` is built by `" ".join(shlex.split(integrator_command(repo))[3:])`, which strips necessary quoting from the command string produced with `shlex.join`. For `repo = Path("/tmp/my repo")`, `integrator_command` returns `... --repo '/tmp/my repo' --agent integrator queue run`; after split/join the tail is `--repo /tmp/my repo --agent integrator queue run`, with no quotes around the path. That unquoted tail is not a suffix of the stored command, so `live_jobs` returns `[]` for a running integrator job. `integrator_alive()` is then false in the interval before the real integrator takes the queue lock, and the 30s tick can start a second integrator job for the same repo, violating the single-flight guarantee that two never run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:live_jobs

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `LR.warning(rp, cfg, st)` without an explicit `now` (or a patched clock) after releasing `T1` moments earlier. The earlier wait test shows `LR.warning` returns `""` when `now - queued_at` has not exceeded `cfg.merge_queue.auto_run_after_s`, and the tick wait test expects `auto_run_after_s` to be at least 1. In a normal fast test run the released entry is not overdue, so `LR.warning` returns `""`, causing `assert "T1 was released and is PARKED" in text` to fail. The test must pass a `now` past `queued_at + auto_run_after_s`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:test_a_parked_released_entry_is_named_with_the_call_that_resumes_it

chunk_findings.detail: `_start_locked` accesses `alive[0].id` when `alive` is non-empty, but `alive` contains whatever `LR.live_jobs(repo, st)` returns (presumably `Job` objects or dictionaries, not strings). If `Job` is a dataclass or NamedTuple without an `.id` attribute (or if it is a dictionary accessed via `.id`), this throws an `AttributeError` or `KeyError` whenever an integrator is already running, which then causes `start_integrator` to fail with an unhandled exception instead of returning the expected `_not_started` dictionary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:59

chunk_findings.detail: The tick decides whether an entry is overdue by calling the host wall clock directly (`LR.overdue(Path(ctx.repo), ctx.cfg, time.time())`), and `start_integrator(..., now=...)` never uses its `now` parameter. In a fake-clock environment (which the project guidance requires for clocks [r-adapters]), this bypasses the injected clock. For example, with `[merge_queue].auto_run_after_s = 1`, an entry released at fake time `1000`, a `TickCtx`/adapter clock of `1002`, and a host wall clock of `0`, `LR.overdue(..., time.time())` receives `0`, returns false, and `integrator_tick` returns `None` instead of starting the integrator or restarting a dead integrator job. Conversely, a fast-forwarded host clock can make the tick start prematurely. The tick should use the tick context’s clock or the clock port, and `now` should be threaded through rather than ignored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:integrator_tick

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_run` declares `strictest=("off", "ddflow starts no process on its own; the queue is run by hand")`, but `strictest` is the strictest allowed value for the knob and must be one of `choices=("on", "off")`. With an org policy that locks `merge_queue.auto_run` to `off`, ddflow sees the strictest value as the tuple `("off", ...)` rather than the string `"off"`, so the lock either fails validation or is never considered satisfied. The project can therefore remain `auto_run = "on"` despite an org requirement that ddflow start no process on its own.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The new `auto_run_after_s` and `auto_run_max_parallel` knobs omit `strictest`, unlike the adjacent `auto_run` knob, so they are not org-lockable as written. An org that must forbid immediate auto-starts can lock `auto_run_after_s` to a minimum delay, and an org that must forbid multiple live integrator jobs can lock `auto_run_max_parallel` to `1`, but there is no strictest value to enforce that. A project can set `auto_run_after_s = 0` or `auto_run_max_parallel = 10` and ddflow will accept it, violating [r-everything-configurable].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:auto_run_after_s, auto_run_max_parallel

chunk_findings.detail: The parked-warning loop reads the queue twice: it builds `newest = {e.item: e.seq for e in MQ.entries(repo)}` and then iterates a second call, `for e in MQ.entries(repo):`. In a concurrent multi-agent run, another process can append a queue entry between those two calls. The second iteration then sees an item that was absent when `newest` was built, and `newest[e.item]` raises `KeyError`. For example, if the queue is empty at the first `MQ.entries(repo)` call and another agent enqueues item `X` before the second call, `newest` is empty, the loop reaches `X`, and `brief`, `queue status`, or `doctor` crash instead of returning a warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:warning

chunk_findings.detail: The new integrator code bypasses adapter ports for environment and clock access: `integrator_command()` reads `sys.executable` directly, and `overdue()` calls `time.time()` directly when `now` is omitted. [r-adapters] requires clocks and environment to go through adapter ports so tests and swaps can replace them. Concretely, a test that advances a fake clock port to a future epoch (for example `queued_at = 10**12`, fake now `10**12 + 2`) but calls `LR.overdue(repo, cfg)` without `now` will compare against the process wall clock; if the host wall clock is the current epoch, `now - e.queued_at` is negative and the entry is wrongly reported as not overdue. Likewise, a fake interpreter port cannot change the interpreter path embedded by `integrator_command()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:integrator_command, overdue

chunk_findings.detail: The “fake” job launcher still starts a real OS subprocess: `fake_launch` calls `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`. The fixture therefore does not replace the external process dependency as the project guidance requires (“tests use a fake instead of … a subprocess”); it only replaces `J.launch` with another real-process launcher. In a CI sandbox or container where child process creation is restricted, every test using `procs` fails inside `fake_launch` with `PermissionError`/`OSError` before any ddflow integrator-trigger code is exercised. The previous finding on this point still stands in the current test file.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:procs [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `integrator_tick` still calls `time.time()` directly, and the `now=` parameter on `start_integrator` is never used. This is the prior fake-clock defect still present: with `[merge_queue].auto_run_after_s = 1`, an entry queued at injected time `1000` and a `TickCtx` time of `1002` but a host wall clock of `0` makes `LR.overdue(Path(ctx.repo), ctx.cfg, time.time())` evaluate `overdue(..., 0)` and return false, so a dead integrator is not restarted by the tick. It also bypasses the clock adapter port required by [r-adapters]. The tick should take the clock from the tick context/adapter or pass `now` through to `start_integrator`/`LR.overdue`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_run` passes `strictest=("off", "ddflow starts no process on its own; the queue is run by hand")`. The `knob` strictest value is expected to be one of the `choices` strings here, i.e. `"off"`, not a two-tuple. A strict-mode config load or validation that checks `strictest in ("on", "off")` rejects the tuple; if it instead stores the tuple, an org lock set to that strictest is not recognized as `"off"`, so the org lock fails and the knob is not actually lockable as intended. This is unchanged from the previous review.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_run_after_s` and `auto_run_max_parallel` omit `strictest`, unlike the adjacent `auto_run` knob. Under [r-everything-configurable] these knobs must be org-lockable, but a project can set `auto_run_after_s = 0` or `auto_run_max_parallel = 10` even when an org policy should forbid immediate auto-start or more than one live integrator job, because there is no strictest value to lock them to. The current diff still lacks both `strictest` arguments.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:53,58

chunk_findings.detail: The previous [r-adapters] finding is still present. `integrator_command()` reads `sys.executable` directly, and `overdue()` reads `time.time()` directly when `now is None`. This bypasses the adapter ports required for environment and clock access, so tests or swaps cannot replace the interpreter path or clock without editing service code, and a fake-clock caller gets the host wall clock.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:integrator_command, overdue

chunk_findings.detail: `warning` calls `MQ.entries(repo)` twice: once to build `newest` and again to iterate the parked-entry check. If an entry is enqueued/released between the two calls (status/brief/doctor are read-only and not serialized with queue writes), the second list can contain an item absent from `newest`, so `newest[e.item]` raises `KeyError` and the whole status/brief/doctor command fails.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:warning

chunk_findings.detail: Still present from the prior review: the `procs` “fake” launcher starts a real OS subprocess (`subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`) instead of a fake job starter. In a CI sandbox or container where child process creation is restricted, every test using `procs` fails inside `fake_launch` before exercising ddflow, and liveness checks depend on real OS process scheduling rather than a fake clock/adapter. This violates [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:procs

chunk_findings.detail: Still present: this test calls `LR.warning(rp, cfg, st)` with no explicit `now` and no patched clock after releasing `T1`. In a normal fast test run the released entry is not overdue (`auto_run_after_s` is at least 1 per the tick-wait test), so `LR.warning` returns `""`, and the assertions `"T1 was released and is PARKED" in text` / `"ddflow claim T1" in text` fail. The test must know it is looking at a late time, or must handle the not-overdue case.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:test_a_parked_released_entry_is_named_with_the_call_that_resumes_it

chunk_findings.detail: The test computes `late = MQ.live(rp)[0].queued_at + cfg.merge_queue.auto_run_after_s + 1`, but calls `MA.queue_status(rp)` before `monkeypatch.setattr(LR.time, "time", lambda: late)`. At the real wall-clock instant just after release the entry is not overdue, so a status command that includes the warning only when overdue will not contain `"warning"` and the assertion fails for any default `auto_run_after_s` larger than the elapsed milliseconds; if status always has a `"warning"` key, the assertion is vacuous and does not verify the required status warning text or next call. The clock patch must be installed before `MA.queue_status`, and the assertion should check the message content.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:test_a_wait_with_nobody_integrating_is_a_warning_with_the_next_call

chunk_findings.detail: `_start_locked` reloads the config under the start lock as `_c` but then ignores it, using the `cfg` loaded before the lock was acquired. The `auto_run` check is also only performed before acquiring `start.lock`. If the knob is changed while a call is waiting on the lock, the call can still start an integrator after the knob has been turned off. For example: process A calls `start_integrator` while `[merge_queue].auto_run = "on"`, then blocks waiting for `start.lock`; during that wait the operator sets `auto_run = "off"`; another process releases the lock without starting anything, and A acquires the lock. `_start_locked` sees waiting entries, uses the stale `cfg.merge_queue.auto_run_max_parallel`, and never rechecks `auto_run`, so it starts a job even though the current config says auto-start is off. That violates the documented “unless … the knob is off” behavior and the “off starts nothing” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:_start_locked

chunk_findings.detail: `integrator_tick` calls `time.time()` directly to decide whether an entry is overdue. Project guidance [r-adapters] requires clocks to go through a port/adapter so tests and runtimes can use a fake or injected clock. With a fake clock set to a time past `[merge_queue].auto_run_after_s`, this tick still uses the real wall clock and can return `None` instead of starting the integrator; conversely, it can start based on real time even when the injected clock says it should not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:integrator_tick

chunk_findings.detail: The knob accepts any integer `>= 1`, so a project can set `[merge_queue].auto_run_max_parallel = 2`. That contradicts the `auto_run` contract in the same section (“none is started while one is alive”) and the stated single-flight design (“a flock or job key so two never run”): with one integrator job already alive and a released entry older than `auto_run_after_s`, the tick fallback is permitted to start a second `ddflow queue run`. Even if the queue lock prevents both from integrating, two integrator processes are now alive and can race the first process’s exit, hold resources, and violate the single-flight guarantee the change says it is adding. The knob should be fixed or upper-bounded to `1` (and org-lockable to `1`) to preserve single flight.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/merge_queue.py:auto_run_max_parallel

chunk_findings.detail: `overdue()` returns every entry in `MQ.QUEUED` once `queued_at` is old enough, without checking that the entry is released or ready. `warning()` then warns whenever `waiting` is non-empty, even if `rel` is empty. Given a merge-queue entry with `state=QUEUED`, `released=False`, `queued_at = now - auto_run_after_s`, no queue lock holder, and no running integrator job, `warning()` returns a non-empty warning like `1 entries waiting (0 released), integrator not running: ddflow queue run` and any fallback using `overdue()` can start the integrator for an entry that is not actually waiting to be integrated. The intent is to warn/start only for released/ready entries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:overdue/warning

chunk_findings.detail: The “fake” job starter is not actually fake: it monkeypatches `J.launch` but then calls `subprocess.Popen` to spawn a real sleeping Python process. This makes the tests depend on process spawning and inherited pytest stdio, and it violates the project rule that external process dependencies go through an adapter/port and that tests use a fake instead of a subprocess [r-adapters]. In a sandbox or CI environment where spawning child processes is restricted, or where pytest capture relies on pipe EOF, this can fail or hang even though the production code under test does not need a real process.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:fake_launch

chunk_findings.detail: `start_integrator` accepts `now: float | None` but never uses it, and `integrator_tick` calls `time.time()` directly instead of a clock port. A call such as `start_integrator(repo, now=0.0)` behaves exactly as if the fake time were not supplied: the time-based check in `integrator_tick` still reads the real clock. This new direct `time` dependency violates [r-adapters], which requires clocks to go through a `ddflow/adapters` port, and makes the intended fake-clock tests ineffective unless tests monkeypatch the module globally.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:start_integrator

chunk_findings.detail: `_start_locked` re-reads the repo config under the start lock (`_l, _c, st = _load(repo, agent)`) but discards `_c` and continues using the stale `cfg` captured before the lock. Interleaving: a process loads `auto_run=on`, waits up to `START_LOCK_WAIT_S` for `start.lock`, while an operator sets `auto_run=off`; when it acquires the lock, `_c` reflects the new `off` value but the old `on` value is used, so the integrator is still started despite the operator turning automatic runs off. This defeats the `auto_run=off` control under concurrent config changes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/mergequeue_start.py:_start_locked

chunk_findings.detail: `overdue` returns every `MQ.QUEUED` entry older than `auto_run_after_s`, not just "released or ready" entries as the trigger contract requires. An item that is enqueued but not yet released and waits longer than the threshold will cause `warning` to report "N entries waiting (0 released)" and will cause `integrator_tick` to start an integrator job even though no released/ready entry is waiting. The caller itself distinguishes `if e.released` when building `rel`, so such unreleased queued entries are expected to appear in this list; they should not trigger auto-run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerelease.py:overdue

chunk_findings.detail: The `procs` fixture teardown unconditionally calls `p.kill()` on every `Popen` in `started`. In `test_a_dead_integrator_job_is_restarted_by_the_tick`, the test itself kills and waits `procs[0]` (lines 77-78). After `wait()`, `Popen.returncode` is set, so the later `p.kill()` in teardown raises `ProcessLookupError`; the test then errors during cleanup even if the actual assertions passed, failing the suite.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `MA.queue_status(rp)` is called before `LR.time` is patched to `late`; with the positive `auto_run_after_s` assumed by line 125, the just-enqueued entry is not overdue. If `queue_status` only includes the `"warning"` key when a warning is active, the assertion fails. If the key is always present, the assertion is vacuous and does not actually verify the required status warning. The clock should be patched before calling `queue_status`, and the assertion should check the warning text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:130-131

chunk_findings.detail: The `procs` fixture uses `subprocess.Popen` directly in `fake_launch`. The project rule r-adapters requires every external dependency, including subprocess tools, to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` and says tests should use a fake instead of a subprocess; this direct OS-process launch is outside that adapter boundary.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_integrator_trigger.py:33 [r-adapters]
